## Decisions

<a id="HowWeMerge"></a>

### How we merge

`HowWeMerge` · `src/sdlc.ts:300` · published

The service's repository, its main branch, merged by a merge commit; what people decide frozen in trame.lock, as Trame publishes it.

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| repository | karim/reservations |
| base | main |
| method | merge |
| lock | trame.lock |
| project | { name: reservations, dir: . } |

- Decided by: karim
- Rejected: Squashed, a pull request that publishes keeps its publication apart from the code it publishes
- Used by: [Our pull requests](#OurPullRequests)

<a id="PullRequestsOnGitHub"></a>

### How a pull request is checked on GitHub

`PullRequestsOnGitHub` · `src/sdlc.ts:244` · published

At each pull request into main, on GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 machine with Node.js 22: its job, named reservations, is a check the repository requires; it writes in it the review of the branch (what its declarations not yet published add to those published), and keeps GitHub from merging a pull request that changes what people decided (a trame.lock of the repository), which a person then merges (D1).

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| on | { pullRequests: main } |
| job | reservations |
| runsOn | ubuntu-24.04 |
| node | 22 |
| artefacts | { days: 30 } |
| pullRequest | { review: true, merge: onceItHoldsUnlessDecided } |

- Decided by: karim
- Rejected: Only when a pull request touches the project, GitHub keeps a pull request waiting for a check it requires and that never ran; Merged by GitHub whatever it changes, what people decided would reach main without a person
- Used by: [Our pull requests](#OurPullRequests)
- Sets the writer of: [The pull requests' workflow](#PullRequestWorkflow)
